title: Stick an adhesive wall hook on its marked spot, level, then press it firmly for 30 seconds
instruction: Stick the hook on the wall, centred on the black cross and level. The strip grabs as soon as it touches, so line it up first. Then press the hook firmly against the wall for 30 seconds and let go.
context: Hanging a 3M Command adhesive hook, which nearly everyone has done. 3M's instructions: press the hook firmly for 30 seconds, then wait an hour before hanging anything. The foam strip grabs on contact, so a hook stuck off its mark or crooked can't be slid into place, only pulled off and redone with a new strip; one pressed too lightly lets go under its load.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, heights above the table. Fixed: a piece of 1/2 in drywall painted light blue (30 x 25 cm) standing on a 9 x 30 x 2 cm wooden foot, its face towards the robot at x 32, from y 0 to 30, 2 to 27 cm up; a black marker cross on it (40 mm strokes, 3 mm wide) centred at (32, 12), 13 cm up; a holder of two tan 12 x 40 x 5 mm blocks with a 5.5 mm slot at (20, 12). Loose: a white 3M Command Medium Utility Hook (17001; 76 x 23 x 25 mm, rated 1.36 kg) standing in the slot on its plate's bottom edge, its foam strip (64 x 19 x 1.6 mm, liner off) towards the wall and its hook towards the robot.
scoring: Stuck: the strip bonded to the wall (it bonds when it lies flat on the wall under at least 1 N, and can't then slide or turn). Place: the plate's middle against the cross's centre; tilt: the plate's turn from upright. Hands clear: no gripper pad or fingertip within 1 cm of the hook. 1.0: stuck within 5 mm of the cross and 3 degrees of level, pressed with at least 10 N for 30 s in all, hands clear. 0.75: stuck on the mark and level but pressed firmly under 30 s, or a hand still on it. 0.5: stuck within 15 mm and 8 degrees. 0.25: stuck anywhere else on the wall. 0: not stuck. Real trial: ruler and level on the plate; time the press; after 1 hour the hook must hold its rated 1.36 kg for 5 minutes.
fidelity: The wall panel sits on a stiff spring (40,000 N/m) whose travel gives the press force; a second counts only while nothing but the hook touches the panel, read from the sim's contacts. The bond is a joint switched on when the strip lies flat on the wall under 1 N; it then holds any load, so the firm 30 s press is scored directly. Strip bonds only flat. Hook 30 g (real about 8 g) for solver stability, made of boxes; liner already off.
reset_notes: Each real trial uses a new strip on a new or cleaned hook; wipe the wall spot with isopropyl alcohol and let it dry. Clamp the wall to the table.
